chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, regarding

the one in Ihram who looked at other than his wife, and discharge descended: he said: Upon him is blood (of a sacrificial animal), because he looked at that which is not permissible for him. And if he did not discharge, then let him fear Allah and not repeat, and there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.غَيْرِ أَهْلِهِ: Non-mahram (women permissible for marriage but not currently married to him)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a person in Ihram who looks at a non-mahram woman?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi, transmitted via Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, distinguishes between mere looking and looking with desire by using sexual discharge as the legal threshold for imposing the penalty of dam (sacrifice). In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the principle that minor sins require vigilance and repentance, while major violations of Ihram restrictions incur tangible expiation, reflecting the nuanced approach to ritual purity and conduct.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar,

‘Regarding the one in Ihraam looking at other than his wife, so his discharge descends. Heasws said: ‘Upon him is blood (of a sacrificial animal), because he looked at other than what is Permissible for him. And, if he did not happen to have discharged, so let him fear Allahazwj, and he should not repeat, and there is nothing upon him’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said

the following: “About a man who in the state of Ihram, looks to those other than his wife and discharges semen, he (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘He owes an animal offering because of looking at what is not lawful for him. If there is no semen discharge, he must maintain piety before Allah, he must not repeat and there is not anything on him.’”
